primary_publications.title: From Gradual Release of Responsibility to Gradual Release of Technology: A Case for the Staged Use of AI in Formal Education
primary_publications.abstract_text: This conceptual article introduces the Gradual Release of AI Technology (GRAIT) model for deciding when and how students should rely on generative AI. It distinguishes who performs cognitive work from when and how that work may be scaffolded, augmented, or offloaded. It proposes three phases: independent cognition, shared cognition with teacher guidance, and offloaded and reallocated cognition. Progression depends on demonstrated knowledge, skill proficiency, epistemic understanding, and AI literacy. The model is a proposed educational framework, not a report of a new experimental test.
primary_publications.abstract_source: Editorial paraphrase checked against the openly available publisher abstract (Education Sciences, 13 August 2026)

framework_notes.idea: AI support should follow demonstrated learning readiness, rather than replace foundational thinking from the outset.
framework_notes.approach: Conceptual synthesis of learning sciences and the staged-use GRAIT framework for formal education.
stages: Independent cognition: develop and demonstrate knowledge without substantive AI assistance
Shared cognition: use AI within guided learning and evaluation
Offloaded and reallocated cognition: delegate selected tasks while retaining judgement
framework_notes.qualification: This paper proposes a conceptual instructional framework; it does not experimentally establish that staged AI access improves outcomes.
